review.material: Read the official issue introduction and complete contents. This is an edited collection, distinct from the Bier–Knight editorial within it.
review.limitations: Individual papers’ methods, results and conclusions were not reviewed as a complete collection; no shared experimental outcome is asserted.

evidence.description: Editorial framing of data-driven design, production and operation

evidence.locator: Contents: opening editorial and five contributed papers

original.label: Read the issue introduction and choose an article

sections.title: In brief
sections.text: The collection examines how data-driven drawing, modeling and simulation relate to artistic and architectural design.

sections.title: Organizing question
sections.text: What happens when computational representations participate in conceptual design, physical production and the subsequent operation of an artifact or building?

sections.title: Editorial premise
sections.text: The introduction emphasizes convergence between computational and material systems, including several possible outcomes from one representation and feedback from users or environments.

sections.title: How it is organized
sections.text: Bier and Knight’s opening editorial introduces five contributions from media studies, art and architecture. Their theoretical discussions and practical experiments remain separate arguments.

sections.title: Reading routes
sections.text: Vehlken examines computational swarming; Moura and Pereira discuss collective robotics in art; Mennan addresses formalism and intuition; Hensel and Sørensen connect data-driven design with local performance-oriented architecture.

sections.title: What this framing establishes
sections.text: The editors propose a feedback loop linking design, production and operation. The collection should be used to compare approaches, rather than treated as one test validating that loop universally.

sections.title: Limits
sections.text: An issue description cannot establish the empirical strength of every contribution. Read each paper for its specific evidence, assumptions and scope.

sections.title: Why browse it
sections.text: It helps separate a computational representation from its multiple realized outputs and from the later interactions that may change them.
